subsystems.name: Legal knowledge base
subsystems.role: Stores the formal, machine-readable version of statutes, definitions and their relationships.

subsystems.name: Rules engine / smart contract platform
subsystems.role: Executes the encoded legal rules against facts to produce decisions or actions.

subsystems.name: Formal verification and testing suite
subsystems.role: Proves that the code faithfully implements the statute and has no contradictions or gaps.

subsystems.name: Data integration layer
subsystems.role: Feeds the engine with facts from registries, sensors, forms and other systems.

subsystems.name: Decision and enforcement module
subsystems.role: Issues outputs such as permits, penalties or compliance flags, with an audit trail.

subsystems.name: Explainability and audit interface
subsystems.role: Lets humans understand and challenge automated decisions.

buildSteps.title: Extract legal rules
buildSteps.detail: Lawyers and engineers read the statute and identify conditions, obligations, exceptions and definitions.

buildSteps.title: Formalize in a machine-readable language
buildSteps.detail: Encode the rules as logical clauses, decision tables or a domain-specific language such as Catala.

buildSteps.title: Implement as executable code
buildSteps.detail: Translate the formal rules into smart contracts or a rules engine, with clear versioning and provenance.

buildSteps.title: Verify against the source law
buildSteps.detail: Use theorem provers, model checkers and test cases to check consistency, completeness and fidelity to the original text.

buildSteps.title: Integrate data sources
buildSteps.detail: Connect registries, APIs and user input so the engine receives the facts it needs to apply the rules.

buildSteps.title: Deploy in a controlled pilot
buildSteps.detail: Run alongside human decision-makers, compare outcomes, and fix discrepancies before scaling.

buildSteps.title: Scale with oversight
buildSteps.detail: Expand to more rules, add appeal and audit mechanisms, and keep humans in the loop for contested cases.

prerequisites.why: theorem provers and model checkers exist, but encoding open-textured legal concepts remains unsolved.
blockchain platforms can execute deterministic code, though they are not designed for legal nuance.
efforts such as LegalRuleML and OASIS LegalDocumentML exist but are not widely adopted.
secure digital IDs and APIs are available in many jurisdictions, enabling fact-finding.
explanation methods are immature for rule-based systems, and legal appeal processes are not automated.

pathway.milestone: rules-as-code pilots in tax, benefits and licensing, such as New Zealand's Better Rules and France's Etalab
pathway.unlocks: automated compliance for well-defined, high-volume rules.

pathway.milestone: standardized legal encoding languages and verification tooling
administrative decision automation with mandatory human review
pathway.unlocks: faster, more consistent routine decisions in government.

pathway.milestone: judiciary automation for narrow domains, with appeal to human courts
pathway.unlocks: reduced backlogs, but requires new legal frameworks for liability and due process.
